raw_response:
My whole life I have grown wheat and corn on this land. My father grew wheat and corn. My sons grew up watching me grow wheat and corn. I am 70 years old now and my back is not what it was, so I am not going to start trying something new. The land here is flat and the well is still working. That is enough.

I have about 10 mu. I will plant all of it in winter wheat come October, then turn it over to summer corn after harvest in June. That is what everyone in the village does. That is what makes sense here.

For wheat seeds, I will buy the improved seeds from the township supply station — the kind the village head said most people are using now. Not the old stuff I saved myself, because the last two years the yields were a bit lower with saved seed. But I am not going to pay extra for some fancy new hybrid either — too expensive and I do not know if it will do better on my ground.

For fertilizer I will put down a good base dressing before planting — I always put a bit extra to be safe. Better to have too much than a thin crop. I will irrigate three times for the wheat: once before winter sets in, once when it joints, once when it heads out. For corn in summer I might only need one or two waterings if the rains come.

I will spray herbicide in spring and do one pesticide treatment if I see aphids or blight. I have done this for fifty years. I know what to look for.
